distr continuous, positive¶

Families for positive quantities: lifetimes, waiting times, sizes, amplitudes and the distributions of test statistics. Each page documents one family: the parameters, the support, how to evaluate the density and the distribution function, how to draw samples, and, for the families that have one, the object form and the maximum-likelihood fit.

The Surface¶

Family

What it is

Alpha

The alpha distribution: a positively skewed distribution on the positive axis whose density is a normal density in the reciprocal of the variable.

Burr

The Burr (type III) distribution: a flexible heavy-tailed distribution on the positive axis with two shape parameters.

Chi

The chi distribution: the distribution of the length of a vector of independent standard normal variables.

ChiSquare

The chi-squared distribution: the distribution of a sum of squared independent standard normal variables.

ChiSquareNoncentral

The noncentral chi-squared distribution: the distribution of a sum of squared independent normal variables whose means are not zero.

Erlang

The Erlang distribution: the waiting time until the k-th event of a Poisson process, a gamma distribution with an integer shape.

Exponential

The exponential distribution: the waiting time between independent events that occur at a constant rate.

F

The F distribution: the distribution of a ratio of two independent chi-squared variables, each divided by its degrees of freedom.

FNoncentral

The noncentral F distribution: the distribution of the F statistic when the numerator has a noncentral chi-squared distribution.

Gamma

The gamma distribution: a flexible family on the positive axis, the sum of exponential waiting times and the parent of the chi-squared family.

Gig

The generalised inverse Gaussian distribution: a three-parameter family on the positive axis that contains the inverse Gaussian, the gamma and the inverse gamma distributions.

Gompertz

The Gompertz distribution: the distribution of adult lifetimes, with a hazard rate that grows exponentially with age.

InverseGaussian

The inverse Gaussian distribution: the distribution of the first time a Brownian motion with positive drift reaches a fixed level.

Lognormal

The lognormal distribution: the distribution of a variable whose logarithm is normal, the standard model of multiplicative growth.

Lomax

The Lomax (Pareto type II) distribution: a power-law distribution that starts at zero, the standard heavy-tailed model of lifetimes and claim sizes.

Maxwell

The Maxwell distribution: the length of a three-dimensional vector of independent zero-mean normal variables, the speed of a gas molecule.

Nakagami

The Nakagami distribution: a flexible model of the amplitude of a fading signal, with a shape parameter that covers more and less severe fading than the Rayleigh case.

Pareto

The Pareto distribution: the power-law distribution of sizes above a minimum, the standard model of wealth, city sizes and insurance losses.

Planck

The Planck distribution: a density proportional to x^a/(exp(b x) - 1), the shape of black-body radiation.

Rayleigh

The Rayleigh distribution: the length of a two-dimensional vector whose components are independent zero-mean normals.

Rice

The Rice distribution: the length of a two-dimensional vector whose mean is offset from the origin and whose components have independent normal noise.

Wald

The Wald distribution: the inverse Gaussian distribution with mean 1.

Weibull

The Weibull distribution: the standard model of lifetimes and failure times, with a hazard that can fall, stay constant or rise.
